# Preface {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-important}
## An AI-directed project, early in its development

Every chapter here was researched and written by Claude, an AI model, working
from the primary literature under human direction. No chapter has yet been read
by a subject expert.

The project is built so that the claims can be checked rather than taken on
trust. Each statement traces back to a record naming the paper it came from and
the lines it was read from, the bibliography is generated from those records,
and several automated checks run on every change. Those checks compare numbers
and wording. They cannot catch a sentence that says slightly more than its
source, and some have got through and been corrected after the fact.

Read this as a referenced starting point rather than as a reviewed secondary
source, and go to the cited paper before relying on anything. Corrections are
welcome as [issues](https://github.com/brianjohnhaas/IsoformBiology/issues).
:::

A gene is not a transcript. Most human genes produce several, sometimes dozens,
and the differences between them are often the biology. Which protein domain is
present, which cell type expresses which form, whether a transcript is
translated at all or routed to decay: these are isoform-level questions, and a
gene-level answer cannot reach them.

Yet most transcriptomic analysis still collapses this to one number per gene.
That collapse is sometimes justified and often simply inherited from a time when
nothing finer was measurable. This book is an argument, built from the primary
literature, that the finer resolution is where a great deal of the biology lives.

It is organized as a book rather than a tool list because the case is cumulative:
landmark examples across the tree of life, the technology arc that made them
visible, the disease biology that depends on isoform-level resolution, and the
current efforts to catalog the isoform universe outright.

::: {.callout-note}
## Status
All twelve chapters are drafted, from research records built one paper at a
time.
The checks that run on every commit, and the things they cannot see, are listed
in [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md).

Four glossary terms rest on no citable source and are written on this book's
own authority. They are marked in place, and they are the entries most in need
of a reader.
:::
